The proposed behavior therefore cannot be documented as current durable behavior.

The current repository documents product-user access administration and customer-facing class APIs, but this source's separate customer-management resource and ghost-to-identity linking rules remain an explicitly in-flight architecture proposal with no implemented customer resource to verify.

Product resolution and membership/access records are product-scoped, but the source asks an open privacy-policy question about a future customer identity and cross-product discovery model. Incidental product scoping does not settle whether or how customer matching must be hidden.

Verification found no customer-receiver user_id API, customer_id API, ghost-customer behavior, or 1.x compatibility horizon in the current API map, code, migrations, SDK, or regression-test source. The checkout identity was also inspected: repository-identity.json reports a remote while target-repo/docs/repositories/structure.md calls the parent documentation folder local-only; that run-evidence contradiction does not establish or alter this customer contract.

The repository uses user_id for the implemented product-user, profile, membership, registration, and role flows, but contains no customer_id replacement surface or SDK-visible migration contract. Immediate replacement safety cannot be established from the current repository.

The handoff asks for a decision to adopt the additive canonical-customer_id transition. No explicit approved durable policy or implemented customer identity contract resolves that decision, so no project-memory change is safe.
